name: The Promise Ring
label: Jade Tree
lede: The Promise Ring grew out of two dead Milwaukee bands and a loaned Cap'n Jazz guitarist, then turned emo into power pop and nearly died doing it: a van through a Nebraska snowstorm, a brain tumor found the day a tour was due to leave, and a last album made to get away from the word.

eras.title: Borrowed from Cap'n Jazz
eras.text: The Promise Ring came out of two dead Milwaukee bands and a guitarist on loan from Chicago's Cap'n Jazz. The loan turned permanent that summer, when Cap'n Jazz broke up in the middle of a tour.

years.h: Two broken Milwaukee bands become one
years.p: Guitarists [[Jason Gnewikow|d6ee8d9d-ef4a-4f96-8e7a-bf5f239c2ac0]] and Matt Mangan of None Left Standing join drummer [[Dan Didier|60e8d768-3d24-446b-b21c-1dffc6fbca7b]] and bassist Scott Beschta of Ceilishrine, and the Promise Ring starts up in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

years.h: Mangan moves to Indianapolis and a Cap'n Jazz guitarist steps in
years.p: Matt Mangan relocates. Gnewikow's friend [[Davey von Bohlen|b1bb1a6c-898b-4d0d-ab0a-6473859d229b]], who plays guitar in [[Cap'n Jazz|04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825]], takes his place.

years.h: Three songs on tape and a friend's label to put them out
years.p: The new line-up's March demo has Jupiter, 12 Sweaters Red and Mineral Point. Mineral Point and Watertown Plank soon come out as a 7-inch on Foresight Records.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz breaks up on day nine of its tour
years.p: Von Bohlen does a ten-day East Coast run with the Promise Ring, then heads out with Cap'n Jazz. When that band splits, he's a full-time Promise Ring member.

eras.title: A tape handed to Jade Tree
eras.text: A friend in Texas Is the Reason passed the demo to Jade Tree, a Delaware label known for hardcore, and the band left with a three-album deal. It didn't think much of its first album. Fans made it an emo standard anyway.

years.h: Norman Brannon hands a tape to Jade Tree
years.p: [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]] guitarist [[Norman Brannon|fbe11657-2638-4486-8369-2157644a9031]] gives the demo and the 7-inch to Jade Tree co-founder Tim Owen. Soon after, Owen signs the band to a three-album contract.
years.xp: Brannon played in Texas Is the Reason, not the Promise Ring. His band later toured with the Promise Ring and shared a split single with it.

years.cap: The Promise Ring in the 1021 8th Street basement, Minneapolis, September 15, 1996
yt: Full set, 1021 8th Street basement, Minneapolis, Sept 15, 1996
years.h: Falsetto Keeps Time is the first Jade Tree release
years.p: The EP lands while the band keeps playing church halls and basements across the US.

years.h: A split single with the band that got them signed
years.p: The Promise Ring shares the release with Texas Is the Reason, whose guitarist Brannon had handed Jade Tree the tape.

q: The wrong recording at the wrong time with the wrong person.
yt: Live at P.W.A.C., Lindenhurst NY, July 1996
years.h: 30° Everywhere gets five days and a sick singer
years.p: Cut at Idful Music in June 1996 with engineer [[Casey Rice|ea30cea0-fb0c-4893-835d-1629e8c1dff3]] while Davey von Bohlen was ill. A Picture Postcard became an emo standard, and the album had sold 12,000 copies by September 1997.
years.xp:
The band was hard on it. Von Bohlen said he'd never listen to the first record, and that they had no idea what they wanted it to sound like.

Fans disagreed. 30° Everywhere made LA Weekly's list of the 20 best emo albums.

years.cap: Davey von Bohlen at a church-basement show, Iowa State
yt: Full set, Mind Over Matter fest, Michigan, March 1997
years.h: Six weeks across the US with Texas Is the Reason
years.p: The tour runs through late 1996. The Promise Ring then crosses to Europe in April and May 1997.

years.h: Scott Beschta leaves after clashing with Dan Didier
years.p: The two fell out during sessions for the second album. Tim Burton, Jason Gnewikow's old None Left Standing bandmate, takes bass for the tour.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts it flatly: the relationship between Didier and Beschta "progressively deteriorated" over the sessions. Beschta was replaced around the time Nothing Feels Good came out.

yt: Why Did Ever We Meet, Fireside Bowl, Chicago, Oct 2, 1998
years.h: Memphis, J. Robbins and Nothing Feels Good
years.p: Recorded in June 1997 at Easley McCain in Memphis with [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]]. It sold in the mid five figures and made best-of lists in the New York Times and Teen People.
years.xp: The sound got poppier without losing the emo core. Darren Doane directed the Why Did Ever We Meet video. The cover photo was shot in front of Trimper's Rides on the boardwalk in Ocean City, Maryland.

eras.title: A windshield and a brain tumor
eras.text: At its peak the band came close to ending twice. A van wreck put the singer through the windshield and the guitarist in intensive care. Two years later a brain tumor, behind 18 months of headaches during shows, cancelled a tour on the day it was due to leave.

years.cap: Davey von Bohlen at a club show, c. 1998
years.h: The van rolls in a Nebraska snowstorm
years.p: On tour with [[Hum|04c5ca8a-4afa-4031-aced-6357440dbc25]], Von Bohlen hits a bump and the van flips. He goes head-first through the windshield, and Gnewikow spends three weeks in intensive care.
years.xp:
Von Bohlen had head trauma. Bassist Tim Burton broke bones, and Gnewikow's injuries included a broken collarbone. Didier was released from hospital the next morning.

The band took six weeks to recover before it played again.

years.h: Scott Schoenbeck takes the bass after the crash
years.p: With Schoenbeck in, the band returns on the East Coast with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]], then tours Europe that summer with [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]].

years.h: Boys + Girls fills the gap
years.p: The stopgap EP carries Tell Everyone We're Dead and Best Looking Boys.

years.h: An acoustic side project called Vermont
years.p: Von Bohlen and Didier start it with Chris Rosenau of [[Pele|eb54e2fe-5477-42ed-a976-f242e51c2895]].

years.h: Living at J. Robbins' house to make Very Emergency
years.p: The band stays at [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]]' home in Silver Spring, Maryland, and records at Inner Ear in Washington, D.C. The album comes out the same day as [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]]' Something to Write Home About.
years.xp:
[[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] and Hilary Soldati of Smart Went Crazy guest. The Emergency! Emergency! video, directed by Darren Doane, premiered on MTV's 120 Minutes in October. Spin put the album among the top 20 releases of 1999.

That fall the band toured the US with Robbins' band [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]], joined on dates by [[Pele|eb54e2fe-5477-42ed-a976-f242e51c2895]] and [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]].

years.cap: Davey von Bohlen at a church-basement show, Iowa State, c. 2000
years.h: A brain tumor cancels the Europe tour on departure day
years.p: On the day the band is due to leave with [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]], von Bohlen is diagnosed with a meningioma. Surgery is on May 8.
years.xp:
He had been getting intense headaches during shows for 18 months. The operation involved removing and reattaching part of his skull. The Electric Pink EP, two Very Emergency outtakes, came out that month.

The band came back in September supporting [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]] for three weeks, but a post-operative infection forced them off the tour.

years.h: Von Bohlen guests on Jimmy Eat World's A Praise Chorus
years.p: The friends from the road trade a favor, and the song becomes a promotional single from Bleed American.

eras.title: Away from emo, then away
eras.text: The Promise Ring left Jade Tree for Epitaph's new Anti- imprint and made a Stephen Street record to get distance from the scene it had helped build. The sessions cost the band a bassist, and von Bohlen fainted at SXSW. Six months after the album came out, it was done.

years.h: The Promise Ring leaves Jade Tree for Anti-
years.p: Jade Tree couldn't give the financial backing the band wanted. After courting from Epitaph Records, the band signs to Epitaph's Anti- imprint.
years.xp: Part of the move was the word itself. On Jade Tree the band had become more and more identified as emo, and it wanted distance from that. For shows with Camden that spring, Camden's William Seidel joined on keyboards.

years.h: Stephen Street goes on vacation and can't be reached
years.p: Mid-project, the [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] producer [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]] is unreachable. Schoenbeck, unhappy with the new direction, quits during the LA sessions and Camden's Ryan Weber takes over.
years.xp: With the budget in trouble, the band split Wood/Water between Street at Jacobs Studios in Farnham, England, and [[Mario Caldato Jr.|92762a95-0762-4604-b5bf-0d4ff3961de3]] in Los Angeles, who produced Say Goodbye Good.

years.h: Von Bohlen faints at South by Southwest
years.p: Von Bohlen collapses at South by Southwest and has another operation over the following weeks. It leaves a plate in his head.

years.h: Wood/Water leaves emo behind
years.p: The fourth album, on Anti-, is a softer, stranger pop record with a Stephen Street sound. The Stop Playing Guitar video was directed by ex-[[GusGus|f5cff7b2-b19d-4934-8525-b17248b30ab3]] members Arni + Kinski.

yt: Become One Anything One Time, Late Night with Conan O'Brien
years.h: Conan O'Brien puts the band on network TV
years.p: Midway through a US tour with [[The Weakerthans|bc68928b-fbb5-4aac-baae-52ba49202372]], the band plays Late Night, then heads to the UK supporting Jimmy Eat World.

years.cap: The Promise Ring on stage, c. 2002
years.h: Epitaph announces the Promise Ring is done
years.p: After closing out the Plea for Peace tour, the band calls it a day. Members said they'd been thinking about it for months, and a planned video for Suffer Never was never filmed.
years.xp: Epitaph and Anti- made the announcement on October 14, 2002. The band said it wanted to focus on other projects.

eras.title: Maritime, and a few Metro nights
eras.text: Von Bohlen and Didier kept playing together as Maritime. The Promise Ring came back for the occasional night, mostly at Chicago's Metro, and ruled out new music.

years.h: Von Bohlen and Didier regroup as In English, later Maritime
years.p: With [[Eric Axelson|ecc42a4f-e214-40f1-af6d-6cdcade19702]] of [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]] they form In English, soon renamed [[Maritime|dbc59d71-6d29-4563-ba89-a60bab1c0f40]]. Anti- passed on the debut, Glass Floor, which DeSoto released in 2004.

years.cap: The Promise Ring at Metro, Chicago, November 12, 2005
years.h: One night at Metro's Flower 15 festival
years.p: The Promise Ring plays a single reunion set at Chicago's Metro.

years.big: "No interest at all to write new music"
q: No interest at all to write new music.
years.h: The reunion is on, and the new songs aren't
years.p: A November 2011 tweet leads to reunion shows, then Bamboozle, Riot Fest and Fun Fun Fun Fest. A rarities set promised for Dangerbird Records never appears.

years.h: Nothing Feels Good, start to finish, on New Year's Eve
years.p: The band plays the whole album at Metro Chicago. Didier says maybe more shows, but definitely not new music.

years.h: Wrecking Ball is the last show on record
years.p: The band plays the festival in 2016. No later appearance is documented.
